presentingComplaint: Three weeks of low-grade fever, night sweats, and progressive fatigue
history: Previously healthy 42-year-old man with a 3-week history of intermittent low-grade fever, drenching night sweats, malaise, anorexia and ~4 kg unintentional weight loss. Reports new exertional breathlessness over the past week. Underwent dental scaling and extraction about 5 weeks ago without antibiotic prophylaxis. Childhood history of rheumatic fever with a known mitral valve murmur. No injection drug use, no prosthetic valve, no recent hospitalization.
examination: Ill-looking, pale. New/changed pansystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla (mitral regurgitation). Splinter haemorrhages in two nail beds, a Janeway lesion on the right palm and tender Osler's nodes on the finger pulps. Mild splenomegaly. Conjunctival petechiae. No neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficit; chest with bibasal fine crackles suggesting early pulmonary congestion.
imaging: Transthoracic echocardiogram shows a 12 mm mobile vegetation on the anterior mitral leaflet with moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation; transoesophageal echo confirms the vegetation and excludes perivalvular abscess.
microbiology: Three sets of blood cultures from separate venepunctures drawn before antibiotics; all three grow viridans group streptococci (Streptococcus sanguinis), penicillin-susceptible — persistently positive, consistent with a typical IE organism.
finalDiagnosis: Infective endocarditis — Duke definite (native mitral valve, viridans streptococci)
citations: AHA Infective Endocarditis: Diagnosis, Antimicrobial Therapy and Management of Complications 2015 (2023 update)
stewardship: Subacute native-valve IE with a typical organism: after 3 sets of blood cultures, start empiric IV therapy pending sensitivities. Reasonable empiric regimen for subacute native-valve disease is IV ampicillin plus a beta-lactamase-stable agent, or for staphylococcal cover vancomycin; here viridans streptococci confirmed penicillin-susceptible, so de-escalate to IV benzylpenicillin (or ceftriaxone) +/- gentamicin for a 4-week course per AHA/ESC. Directed narrow-spectrum therapy on culture and susceptibility is the goal.
contraindications: Aminoglycoside (gentamicin) caution in renal impairment; monitor levels and renal function
Avoid empiric monotherapy that misses staphylococci before cultures return
edgeCases: Culture-negative IE (prior antibiotics, HACEK, Coxiella/Bartonella) — serology and prolonged cultures needed
Right-sided IE in injection drug users presents with septic pulmonary emboli rather than a murmur
Acute S. aureus IE can present fulminantly with valve destruction rather than this subacute picture
expectedMaiK: This is a Duke-definite native-valve infective endocarditis: a typical organism (viridans streptococci) on persistently positive blood cultures plus echocardiographic vegetation and a new regurgitant murmur. Secure at least three sets of blood cultures before antibiotics, obtain echocardiography, and use directed rather than broad empiric therapy while assessing for surgical indications.
expectedNextQuestions: Any recent dental/surgical procedures or injection drug use?
History of valvular disease, prosthetic valve or previous endocarditis?
Any symptoms of embolic events (stroke, limb ischaemia, back pain)?
